questions.question: A student is analyzing the web address https://www.cbse.gov.in/cpanel/index.html. Which part of this URL specifically identifies the protocol and the top-level domain respectively?
questions.explanation: The protocol is 'https' (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) and the top-level domain (TLD) is '.in' (indicating India).
questions.hint: Look for the scheme at the very beginning and the final geographical or organizational extension of the domain name.

questions.question: You are managing a server and need to upload a large batch of backup files from your local computer to a remote web server. Which protocol is most efficiently designed for this specific task?
questions.explanation: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is explicitly designed for the transfer of computer files between a client and server on a computer network.
questions.hint: The acronym stands for exactly what you are doing with the files.

questions.question: When an end-user types a URL into their browser, the browser acts as a client. Which of the following best describes the immediate role of the Web Server in this interaction?

options.text: It converts the HTML code into a visual webpage for the user.
It translates the domain name into an IP address.
It locates the requested webpage files and transmits them back to the client.
It provides the physical internet connection required to access the web.

questions.explanation: A web server processes incoming network requests and sends back the requested resources (like HTML files and images) to the client's browser over HTTP.
questions.hint: Its main job is to "serve" the files that make up the website upon request.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes between the Internet and the World Wide Web (WWW)?

options.text: The WWW is the hardware infrastructure, while the Internet is the collection of linked documents.
The Internet is a massive network of networks, while the WWW is a service of linked pages operating over the Internet.
They are synonymous terms that describe the global system of interconnected computers.
The Internet uses HTTP, whereas the WWW relies entirely on physical cables to transfer data.

questions.explanation: The Internet is the underlying physical network infrastructure. The WWW is an information system built on top of the Internet that allows documents to be connected by hypertext links.
questions.hint: One provides the physical roads; the other is the traffic (information) utilizing those roads.

questions.question: An educator regularly updates a webpage with their personal experiences and tutorials, displayed in reverse chronological order. What is this type of website best categorized as?
questions.explanation: A blog (weblog) is an informational website consisting of discrete, often informal diary-style text entries (posts) typically displayed in reverse chronological order.
questions.hint: The term is a truncated word derived from "weblog".

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'NewsGroup' in internet terminology?

options.text: A commercial news website like NDTV or BBC.
A discussion group on the internet usually focused on a particular topic, operating within the Usenet system.
A social media platform focused solely on sharing daily news articles.
The server hardware that hosts live news broadcasting services.

questions.explanation: Newsgroups are online discussion forums on the Usenet network where users can read and post messages (articles) about specific subjects of interest.
questions.hint: It functions similarly to an old-school digital bulletin board system for niche hobbies or discussions.

questions.question: A new e-commerce startup wants to establish an internet connection for their warehouse. They have the computers, routers, and modems set up. What is the missing critical entity they must subscribe to in order to gain actual access to the internet?
questions.explanation: An ISP (Internet Service Provider) is a company that provides individuals and organizations access to the internet and other related services.
questions.hint: Companies like Jio, Airtel, or local broadband providers serve this specific role.

questions.question: You visit a vegetable delivery app's website where the homepage shows a personalized greeting and product recommendations based on your previous order history. What type of web page are you interacting with?
questions.explanation: A dynamic web page is generated in real-time, often fetching data from a database to display customized content for the user, unlike static pages which look exactly the same for every visitor.
questions.hint: The content changes "on the fly" rather than staying fixed.

questions.question: While reviewing the source code of a webpage, a developer notices links that allow users to jump from one web page to a completely different server's web page. What is the fundamental internet terminology for these clickable links?
questions.explanation: Hypertext refers to text on a display that contains links (hyperlinks) to other texts, forming the core navigational structure of the World Wide Web.
questions.hint: It's the 'HT' in both HTML and HTTP.

questions.question: A user sends an email to a vendor regarding a wholesale order, and then browses a secure online portal to track the shipment. Which combination of protocols was primarily utilized for these two respective actions?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used for sending outgoing emails, and HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure) is used for secure web browsing over encrypted connections.
questions.hint: One protocol is specifically designed for pushing mail outward, and the other is the secure version of web document transfer.

questions.question: An online feedback form requires a user to select only one rating from "Excellent", "Good", "Average", and "Poor". Which HTML input type is most appropriate to ensure they cannot select more than one option simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Radio buttons are used in HTML forms when a user must select one and only one option from a mutually exclusive set of choices. Checkboxes would allow multiple selections.
questions.hint: Think of old car stereos where pushing one preset button automatically pops the other ones out.

questions.question: While designing a web page for a school timetable, a student wants the 'Recess' cell to stretch across three consecutive columns. Which attribute should be added to the <td> tag to achieve this?
questions.explanation: The colspan attribute in HTML is used to make a single table cell span across multiple columns horizontally.
questions.hint: The name of the attribute is a contraction of "column span".

questions.question: A student finds a well-written essay on the internet, copies it entirely, and submits it to their teacher for grading under their own name. What specific unethical practice has the student committed?
questions.explanation: Plagiarism is the act of taking someone else's work, ideas, or writing and passing them off as one's own without proper attribution or permission.
questions.hint: It involves "stealing" intellectual property or academic work rather than technical data.

questions.question: A recipe blog needs to display the steps to bake a cake in a specific, numbered order (1, 2, 3...) so readers do not mix up the sequence. Which HTML tag should be used to enclose these list items?
questions.explanation: The <ol> (ordered list) tag is used to create lists where the sequence of items is important, typically displayed automatically with numbers or letters.
questions.hint: The 'o' in the tag name stands for "ordered".

questions.question: You receive an urgent text message claiming your bank account will be suspended unless you immediately click a provided link and verify your PIN. The link directs you to a fake website that looks identical to your bank. What is this type of attack called?
questions.explanation: Phishing is a social engineering cyber attack where attackers disguise themselves as a trustworthy entity to trick victims into revealing sensitive personal information like passwords or PINs.
questions.hint: It sounds identical to a popular outdoor activity involving a rod, a hook, and bait.

questions.question: How can you create a link in HTML that, when clicked, automatically opens the user's default email program addressed to "info@school.com"?
questions.explanation: The mailto: scheme placed within the href attribute of an anchor (<a>) tag tells the web browser to launch the default email client and prepare an email to that address.
questions.hint: Look for the specific prefix that literally means "mail to".

questions.question: A software developer creates a new, unique mobile application and wants to ensure that no one else can legally copy, sell, or distribute it without permission. Which legal right primarily protects their original software code?
questions.explanation: Copyright provides legal protection to the creators of original works, including software code, literature, and art, preventing unauthorized copying or distribution.
questions.hint: The term itself implies giving the creator the exclusive "right to copy" the work.

questions.question: A science teacher wants to display the chemical formula for water, H2O, on a class website. Which HTML tag is necessary to place the number '2' slightly below the normal line of text?
questions.explanation: The <sub> tag defines subscript text, which appears half a character below the normal typography line and is standardly used in chemical formulas.
questions.hint: Think of a "submarine" that goes below the surface.

questions.question: When completing an online transaction, a user notices the website URL begins with "https://" instead of "http://". What does the "s" signify, and what is its primary purpose?

options.text: System; to ensure the server doesn't crash
Secure; to encrypt data between the browser and server
Speed; to make the transaction process faster

questions.explanation: The "s" stands for Secure. HTTPS uses SSL/TLS encryption protocols to ensure that sensitive data (like credit card numbers) transferred between the user's browser and the web server cannot be intercepted by hackers.
questions.hint: It means your connection is safe from prying eyes.

questions.question: Which HTML5 tag allows a web developer to embed a movie clip directly into a webpage without relying on third-party plugins like Flash?
questions.explanation: The HTML5 <video> element was introduced as the standard native way to embed video content directly into a document.
questions.hint: It uses the most direct and common term for moving digital footage.

questions.question:
A web developer wants all the paragraphs (

) on a multi-page website to use the same font and text color. What is the most efficient way to achieve this without rewriting code on every single page?

options.text:
Add an inline style attribute to every

tag.
Use an internal <style> block in the <head> of each HTML file.
Create an external CSS file and link it to all HTML pages using the <link> tag.
Use the <font> tag inside every paragraph element.

questions.explanation: External Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) allow you to write styling rules once in a separate .css file. By linking this single file to multiple HTML pages, you can control the entire website's design efficiently.
questions.hint: Think about how you can write the rule only one time for the entire website.

questions.question: You are designing a login page for a school portal. Which HTML input type must you use for the password field so that the user's keystrokes are masked (e.g., turned into dots or asterisks) to prevent "shoulder surfing"?
questions.explanation: The password input type behaves exactly like a single-line text field, except that the characters are masked by the browser to protect sensitive information from onlookers.
questions.hint: The type name is exactly the kind of data you are trying to protect.

questions.question: A user legally purchases a proprietary software CD. They install it on their personal laptop, but then give the CD to three friends so they can install it for free. What specific cyber ethics violation does this represent?
questions.explanation: Software piracy involves the unauthorized copying, distribution, or use of proprietary software. Purchasing one license does not grant the right to distribute it to others.
questions.hint: It is the digital equivalent of illegally copying and selling a movie.

questions.question: When you type a query into a search engine like Google, what exactly are you searching through?

options.text: A live, real-time connection of every computer currently online.
A massive, pre-built index of web pages stored on the search engine's servers.
The local cache stored on your personal Internet Service Provider (ISP).

questions.explanation: Search engines use web crawlers (spiders) to scan the internet in advance, building a massive database (index) of keywords and content. When you search, you are actually querying this indexed database, not the live web.
questions.hint: Think of it like looking at the index at the back of a textbook rather than reading every page to find a word.

questions.question: You are building an HTML table for a class roster. You want the top row (containing "Name" and "Roll Number") to stand out. Which tag is semantically correct for defining these header cells, and what default styling does the browser apply?

options.text: <th>, makes the text bold and centered.

questions.explanation: The <th> (table header) tag is used to denote a header cell in an HTML table. By default, all major web browsers render the text inside a <th> tag as bold and center-aligned.
questions.hint: Look for the tag that represents "Table Heading".

questions.question: A developer writes the following CSS in their stylesheet: h1 { color: red; }. However, when they test the webpage, the h1 text appears green. Which of the following is the most likely reason for this styling conflict?

options.text: The browser does not support the color red.
An inline style, such as <h1 style="color: green;">, is overriding the stylesheet.
HTML tags cannot be styled using CSS.
The HTML page is missing the <body> tag.

questions.explanation: In the CSS hierarchy (Cascading), inline styles (styles applied directly inside the HTML tag) have the highest priority and will override internal or external stylesheet rules.
questions.hint: The style closest to the actual element always wins the conflict.

questions.question: Which of the following passwords would take a brute-force hacking algorithm the longest time to crack, making it the most secure choice?
questions.explanation: A strong password includes a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, and avoids common dictionary words or predictable sequences. Option C meets all these criteria, creating high entropy.
questions.hint: Look for the most random combination of different character types.

questions.question: You want to add a background audio track to your webpage that automatically starts playing exactly when the page loads and loops continuously. Which attributes must be included in the <audio> tag?
questions.explanation: The autoplay boolean attribute tells the browser to start playing the audio as soon as it is ready, and the loop attribute tells it to start over again every time it reaches the end.
questions.hint: The attributes are literal terms for "play automatically" and "repeat in a circle".

questions.question: A student is shopping on an e-commerce website. They add a book to their digital cart, close the browser, and return the next day to find the book is still sitting in their cart. What web technology makes this memory retention possible?
questions.explanation: Cookies are small text files stored on the user's computer by the web browser while browsing a website. They are used to remember stateful information, such as items in a shopping cart or login status.
questions.hint: It's a sweet digital "crumb" left behind to remember you.

questions.question: You have coded a very long webpage and want to create a "Back to Top" link at the very bottom. Assuming there is an element at the top of the page with the attribute id="top", how do you correctly format the anchor tag?
questions.explanation: To link to a specific section on the same webpage (an internal bookmark), you use the # symbol followed by the id of the element you want to jump to within the href attribute.
questions.hint: You need the symbol commonly referred to as a hashtag to target an ID.

questions.question: A travel agency website needs a form where users can select their destination country. To save screen space, the developer wants a clickable menu that drops down to reveal the list of countries. Which HTML tags must be combined to create this?
questions.explanation: The <select> tag creates the drop-down list itself, and the <option> tags are nested inside it to define the individual choices available in the list.
questions.hint: You "select" from a list of "options".

questions.question: A web designer notices that the text inside a clickable button is touching the edges of the button's border, making it hard to read. Which CSS property must they increase to create breathing room inside the button, between the text and the border?
questions.explanation: In the CSS Box Model, 'padding' generates space around the content inside an element's border. 'Margin' generates space outside the border, pushing other elements away.
questions.hint: Think of it like the soft material placed inside a helmet to cushion your head.

questions.question: A student is coding a "Contact Us" page and needs to provide a large box for users to type out detailed complaints or feedback spanning several paragraphs. Which HTML tag is designed specifically for multi-line text input?
questions.explanation: The <textarea> tag defines a multi-line text input control. Unlike <input type="text"> which only allows a single line, a textarea can accommodate unlimited lines of text and can be resized.
questions.hint: The tag name literally describes an "area" for "text".

questions.question: When paying on an e-commerce website, a user notices a padlock icon next to the URL. This indicates the site uses digital certificates to encrypt data. Which underlying security protocol enables this encryption?
questions.explanation: SSL (Secure Sockets Layer) and its modern successor TLS (Transport Layer Security) are cryptographic protocols designed to provide communications security over a computer network, forming the basis of HTTPS.
questions.hint: It's an acronym that stands for Secure Sockets Layer.

questions.question: A user browses a social media app for an hour without liking, commenting, or posting anything. However, the app's servers still record their location, device type, and how long they lingered on specific videos. What type of digital footprint is the user generating?
questions.explanation: A passive digital footprint is created when data is collected about a user without their active or intentional participation, often happening behind the scenes via cookies, IP tracking, or analytics.
questions.hint: The user is not "actively" doing anything to leave this data behind.

questions.question: A blogger wants to visually separate their article into two distinct thematic sections by drawing a horizontal line across the web page. Which empty HTML element should be used?
questions.explanation: The <hr> (Horizontal Rule) tag defines a thematic break in an HTML page and is most often displayed as a horizontal line. It is an empty element, meaning it does not have an end tag.
questions.hint: The tag stands for "Horizontal Rule".

questions.question: A developer wants to style exactly three specific warning paragraphs on a webpage to have a red background, while leaving the other fifty paragraphs untouched. Which HTML attribute should they assign to those three paragraphs to use as a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: The class attribute is used to define equal styles for elements with the same class name. The id attribute must be unique to a single element on a page, so it cannot be used for all three.
questions.hint: You use this to group multiple students into one learning room.

questions.question: A hospital is implementing a system where expert surgeons can control robotic surgical arms remotely over the internet to operate on patients in different cities. Which cellular network technology is strictly required for this due to its ultra-low latency (minimal delay)?
questions.explanation: While 4G is fast, 5G networks are designed to provide ultra-low latency (often under 10 milliseconds). This near-instantaneous response time is a strict necessity for critical, real-time applications like remote surgery or autonomous vehicles.
questions.hint: It is the current state-of-the-art generation of cellular networks.

questions.question: A student needs an image for a school presentation and wants to use one legally without paying royalties or worrying about strict copyright infringement. What type of license should they filter their image search by?
questions.explanation: Creative Commons licenses allow creators to grant permission for others to use, share, and sometimes modify their work legally and for free, provided the user follows specific conditions (like crediting the author).
questions.hint: It implies the work belongs to the "commons" (the public) in a "creative" way.

questions.question: A school upgrades its computer lab and throws 40 old desktop towers and CRT monitors into a standard municipal trash dumpster. What specific cyber ethics and environmental issue does this action violate?
questions.explanation: E-waste (Electronic waste) contains highly toxic chemicals and heavy metals (like lead and mercury). Disposing of them in regular landfills is an ethical and environmental violation; they must be sent to certified e-waste recycling centers.
questions.hint: It refers to the garbage generated by electronic devices.
